## Búzios from the Sea

Búzios lies on a peninsula where the coastline constantly changes direction. Beyond each headland, another bay appears; beaches stretch along the water, and green hillsides reach down to the sea. A boat trip reveals this variety in full and shows why this small resort deserves more than a passing glance.

Búzios also has its own urban appeal: low-rise buildings, restaurants and the famous Rua das Pedras. The town grew from a coastal settlement and has retained its close connection to the sea. Out on the water, your attention shifts from signs and café tables to the curves of the coastline and the colours of the bays. The precise boat route depends on conditions during the trip.

The excursion includes a boat trip and suits anyone who wants to add a day by the ocean to their visit to Brazil. Bring a hat, sun protection and a light jacket for the breeze on board. Swimming stops, meals and additional services depend on the terms of the selected programme.

## Excursion Terms

Price: $85 per person. Discounts may be available for more than one person; contact us to discuss.

Breakfast at the hotel.

Excursion to Cajas National Park and a visit to a cacao plantation.

Duration of the excursion day (including transfers): 8–9 hours.
Maximum altitude on the route: 3,900 m above sea level.

Overnight altitude: 0 m above sea level.

Average temperature in Cajas National Park: approximately +10 °C.

After breakfast, we will travel to Cajas National Park, one of Ecuador's most beautiful natural areas, located just 30 km from Cuenca in Azuay Province.

The park covers more than 28,000 hectares and is known for its distinctive high-altitude páramo ecosystem, scenic valleys, rocky landscapes and numerous lakes, with over 250 bodies of water. In recognition of its rich flora and fauna as well as its archaeological value, the area was designated a national park in 1996.

Cajas is striking for its unusual scenery: gentle green plains covered with grasses and rare cushion plants, which play an important role in retaining water, create a distinctive Andean landscape. During our walk, we can enjoy fresh mountain air, admire the lakes and perhaps spot local wildlife, including hummingbirds, mountain toucans and other rare birds.

We will climb to one of the park's best-known locations, Tres Cruces (Three Crosses), a natural watershed from which water flows towards both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans. It is considered one of the region's most impressive viewpoints.

After visiting the park, we will continue towards Guayaquil.

On the way, we will visit a traditional cacao hacienda set amid dry tropical forest. This agritourism estate covers approximately 15 hectares and grows one of Ecuador's most important products: its famous cacao.

During the visit, we will learn about the entire production process, from growing and harvesting the pods to processing cacao beans and making real chocolate. We will explore traditional methods used by local producers and learn how Ecuadorian cacao is prepared for export.

Here we will have a chance to make our own chocolate paste, take part in the preparation and taste authentic hot chocolate.

Lunch at the hacienda is included.

In the afternoon, the route continues to Guayaquil (approximately 3.5 hours on the road).

On arrival, check in at the hotel. The evening is free.

Main stops: Cajas National Park, viewpoints, lakes and páramo landscapes, a cacao plantation and a chocolate workshop.
